titulo: AI inventory: everything the company uses, with an owner
lead: No one protects what they don't know exists. The inventory is the list of everything that uses AI in the company: apps, agents, integrations, spreadsheets that feed the AI, and the tools employees use on their own. Every row has an owner. Without an inventory, the triage in lesson 3 becomes a guess.
objetivo: list apps, agents, integrations, MCP connectors, and the company's shadow AI, with one owner per item, in a single spreadsheet.

aprende.t: The 6 places where AI shows up in a small business
How to find "shadow AI" without breaking into anything
The columns triage will need later
The inventory spreadsheet, ready to copy

hero_alt: A person seen from behind fills in a large sheet with columns, pinned to the wall and covered in colorful sticky notes.

secoes.titulo: Where AI shows up in an SMB
secoes.sub: Six places. Each one becomes rows in the inventory. Tap to see what to look for.

nos.detalhe: Websites and apps that someone put together with AI tools (Lovable, Replit, Bolt and similar). At Horizonte: the order app. Ask who built it, where it is published, and what database it uses.
AI that answers and does things on its own: it handles WhatsApp chats, creates orders, sends emails. At Horizonte: the sales agent on WhatsApp. Write down what it can do, not just what it answers.

Links between the AI and other systems: automations, MCP connectors (the standard that connects the assistant to email, calendar, and Drive). At Horizonte: the MCP integration with email. Write down the permissions for each one.
Tools that employees use without IT knowing: an AI chat on a personal account, a browser extension that reads the screen, a meeting transcriber. It is usually the biggest part of the inventory.
Spreadsheets, folders, and databases that the AI reads or that get pasted into it. At Horizonte: the customer spreadsheet with CPF and phone numbers. Write down who has access and how it is shared.
Whoever processes the data: the API that writes the support summary, the model behind the agent. Write down the country and whether a contract exists. This feeds lesson 6.

secoes.legenda: Old integrations count too: a connector nobody updates keeps its access until someone turns it off.
secoes.dica: Scope: you collect information and ask questions. You do not install spy software, and you do not read anyone's email.

secoes.titulo: How to collect it, in four moves
secoes.sub: Nothing here requires breaking in. It is all asking questions and looking at dashboards with the access owner next to you.

texto: Send a 5-question questionnaire to everyone, with no witch hunt: "what AI do you use at work, for what, with what data, on which account?".
Say that the goal is to protect, not to punish. Without that, shadow AI stays hidden.

exemplo.texto: In the survey, someone in Sales says they paste the customer spreadsheet into a free chatbot, on a personal account, to write proposals. IT did not know.

passos.sub: with the owner next to you
texto: In the company's Google or Microsoft account, the administrator shows the "connected apps": every AI app that asked for access to email or Drive appears there.
Also ask for the corporate card statement for the last 3 months: an AI subscription shows up as a charge.

exemplo.texto: Rafael, can you open the connected apps screen of the company account while I take notes?

texto: For each agent and integration, open the settings screen with the person who administers it and write down what it can do: read, create, send, delete, pay.
This also applies to browser extensions: what they ask for has to match what they promise.

exemplo.texto: The MCP integration with email has permission to send and delete messages. This goes in the "actions" column.

texto: Every item needs an owner: the person who answers if something goes wrong and who can turn it off.
An item without an owner is a finding in itself. Write down "no owner" and take it to the report.

exemplo.texto: The owner is a person with a name, not "sales" or "IT."

We are mapping the company's AI tools so we can use them safely.
No one will be punished for answering. It takes 3 minutes.

1. What AI tools do you use at work? (chat, extension,
   meeting transcription, image generator, other)
2. What for? Give an example of a task.
3. Do you put customer, employee, or financial data into them?
   [ ] no  [ ] sometimes  [ ] always  — what type?
4. Is the account the company's or personal? Paid or free?
5. Does any of them have access to your email, calendar, Drive, or WhatsApp?

abas.html:
1. Every item has an owner with a person's name (or the finding "no owner").
  2. The "actions" column uses verbs: read, create, send, delete, pay.
  3. Each row says where the information came from.
  4. There is at least one item with "IT knows? no".

• Only what IT knows: the inventory comes out neat and incomplete. Shadow AI shows up in the questionnaire and in the invoice.
  • Writing down what the AI says, not what it does: the risk is in the actions (send, delete, give a discount).
  • A "verify" that is never verified: in the report it becomes "not verified," with the reason.

secoes.sub: In the lab company. Failures in this lesson: F12 (shadow AI) and, in passing, F9 (MCP permissions).

exercicios.titulo: 1 · Horizonte inventory with at least 10 items
exercicios.texto: Open the lab IT inventory: Rafael's official list and, below it, the 22 answers from the internal survey. Build your spreadsheet with the AI tools from the official list and the 4 that show up only in the answers (F12). Fill in owner, data, actions, and "IT knows?".
exercicios.pronto: the spreadsheet has at least 10 rows, each with an owner (or "no owner"), and the 4 shadow tools are marked "IT knows? no".

exercicios.texto: In the piece pecas/mcp-email/ (file mcp.json), write down in the "actions" column everything the integration can do and whether there is human approval (F9).
exercicios.pronto: the MCP row says "read, send, delete" and "human approval: no".

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What is the best way to find shadow AI in a small or midsize business?
opcoes: Install a program that monitors the computers.
Questionnaire with no punishment + connected apps from the company account + credit card statement.
perguntas.explica: These are three sources that don't intrude on anything. Monitoring or reading email is out of scope. Asking only IT is the common mistake: shadow AI is exactly what IT doesn't know about.

perguntas.p: What is an MCP connector in the inventory?
opcoes: A link that gives the assistant access to another system (email, calendar, Drive), with its own permissions.
perguntas.explica: MCP is the standard that connects the assistant to other systems. What matters to the auditor is the permissions: read, send, delete.

perguntas.p: An inventory item has no owner. What do you do?
opcoes: Write "no owner" and treat it as a finding in the report.
perguntas.explica: With no owner, no one answers for it or shuts it off. That is a risk in itself. "IT" is not a person, and the owner can't be the auditor.

perguntas.p: In the "actions" column for the WhatsApp agent, what goes in?
opcoes: The verbs for what it can do: reply, give a discount, create an order.
perguntas.explica: The risk is in what the agent does, not in what it says. Discounts and orders involve money: they will weigh in the triage.

itens.texto: Apps built by AI, agents, integrations and MCP, shadow AI, databases and spreadsheets, vendors.
Ask, check accounts, check connectors, confirm the owner.
In May 2026, researchers studying shadow AI found about 380,000 public apps built on vibe coding platforms, around 5,000 of them with sensitive corporate data (recorded on OECD.AI, based on Axios).
Assessment and triage of AI risks. This is not a pentest, nor incident response, nor a legal opinion. Sign of an intrusion, a leak, or a legal question: stop and escalate.
